submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 3.5 cm gives the highest pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c of any configuration simulated: 4.638 sigma. This beats R1 at 4.0 cm (4.601), R1 at 3.0 cm (4.406), and every R2 and R3 thickness (best R2 is 3.786 sigma at 2 cm; best R3 is 2.914 sigma at 3 cm). Separation for R1 peaks around 3.5-4 cm and falls off at 5 and 6 cm, so 3.5 cm sits at the optimum within the 1-6 cm range. The lifetime constraint is not fully verified. The recorded checks report 6 documents read, 0 lifetime-relevant, and 0 with aging content, so no candidate was excluded or flagged. I did not independently confirm that absence, and the project documents contain no measured aging or long-term performance data for R1. Confirm R1 radiator stability over the experiment's lifetime before committing.
